items.title: Update rel261_203 protocol and Undead Rising Season Pass
items.body:
## Summary

This update brings the server’s default protocol configuration in line with client release 261_203. It adds the matching command ID table and updates the related configuration, packaging, and documentation.

It also configures the Undead Rising Season Pass event to grant rewards from the event’s alternate reward slots, so claimed awards match the active event data.

### New Release NPC interaction initialization fix

A recent issue made several Kingshill NPCs (including Grima, Gnob, Thabo, Zumpe, and Petyax) intermittently unavailable for interaction on first entry. In some cases, leaving and re-entering the character made an NPC clickable, which pointed to an initialization/order-of-events problem rather than a consistently missing NPC definition.

The client and server `static.db4` files were verified to have the same SHA-256 hash, and the affected NPC templates had `NoTalk = 0`. This ruled out a client/server static database mismatch and the NPC non-interactive flag as causes.

The map initialization sequence now registers NPC actor IDs in a separate reliable, ordered `ActorsEnterVicinity` frame before player initialization. It also sends the map `EventUpdate` before the corresponding NPC `NewNPC`/`NPCInfo` pairs and before `PlayerReady`. This keeps the client’s actor and map-event state synchronized when it builds NPC interaction targets on initial map entry.

An English troubleshooting note documenting the symptoms, investigation, likely failure mode, and mitigation is included at `docs/NPC_INTERACTION_INITIALIZATION_ORDER.md`.

items.body:
**Benchmark**

`agentic_if` measures whether a coding agent follows instructions while it completes a real repository task
(Scale-SWE) or terminal task (Terminal-Bench format). Each task pairs the work with synthetic instructions about how to do it. The task's own verifier gives `reward`, and an LLM judge plus deterministic checkers grade the recorded session against each instruction.

- 585 tasks. The rows are in an internal registry
- The `example` split holds 5 public tasks (3 from Terminal-Bench 2.1, 2 from Scale-SWE) whose synthetic instructions exercise the same features.

**Linked issue**
None: this adds a new benchmark.


**Validation**

- Gym's onboarding commands, on a fresh Linux copy of the evidence commit with the real prepared data, all exit 0:
  `gym eval prepare --benchmark agentic_if` (585 tasks and the OpenCode runtime files; every SHA-256 pin matches),
  `gym env validate agentic_if --kind benchmark`, `gym env test agentic_if --kind benchmark` (the verifier fixture's
  3 cases), `gym env publish agentic_if --kind benchmark` and `gym env test --resources-server agentic_if`.
- CI's changed-server tests, `ng_test +entrypoint=<dir> +should_validate_data=true`, on Linux at the evidence commit
  for `resources_servers/agentic_if`, `responses_api_agents/opencode_agent`, `resources_servers/scale_swe` and
  `resources_servers/swebench`: all pass.
- On macOS at this PR's head: `resources_servers/agentic_if` (900 passed), `opencode_agent` with
  `tests/unit_tests/test_agent_sessions.py` (656 passed, 49 Linux-only tests skipped), `scale_swe` (107 passed) and
  `benchmarks/agentic_if/tests` (14 passed).
- Coverage of `resources_servers/agentic_if`: 97% (Gym's add-benchmark skill asks for 95%).
- `pre-commit run` on every changed file (the private guardwords catalog is read only in CI), and DCO sign-off.
- `gym dataset collate --mode example_validation` of the example split matches the committed `example_metrics.json`.
- The boundary plugin's 35 golden fixtures match the Python implementation it replaces, byte for byte: request bytes,
  replies, call records and issues.

**Frontier Eval onboarding guide's exit checks**

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| EC-1 health | `gym eval health-check` on the evidence run: 5 healthy, 0 unhealthy, 0 unobserved, no check ignored. `quality_summary.json` has 5 of 5 records, 0 missing. The run used 5 internal probe rows that cover every task feature, a vLLM-served Nemotron 3.5 Super, OpenSandbox sandboxes and the in-sandbox OpenCode binary |
| EC-2 evidence gate | `scripts/inspect_harness_conformance.py --require-sandbox`: exit 0, TE-1 to TE-9 each fulfilled on 5 of 5 rollouts. A run that forced compaction fulfills them on 5 of 5 as well (18 compactions) |

| EC-7 Frontier Eval configs | The leaf composes on all four clusters Frontier Eval runs Gym benchmarks on. Frontier Eval's certification dry run composes it at the evidence commit and judges the evidence run: all four metric keys resolve and 0 of 5 rollouts are unhealthy. It stops on the expected provenance mismatch, since the run was not launched from the leaf (the config change is in Frontier Eval's internal repository) |

**Rollout evidence**

- `resources_servers/agentic_if/data/example_rollouts.jsonl`: five rollouts of the example split from this PR's code,
  served by vLLM, all completed and unmasked. Reward / `if_all`: prawcore 1 / 1, pystow 1 / 0, fix-git 1 / 1,

items.title: Phase 1: neural brain core and cerebellum-driven player movement
items.body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"Memento-craft"} -->
_Requested by **Joshua** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_0158gFjiHmC8khHoguophGYQ?thread=cmsg_0158gFjiHmC8khHoguophGYQ7MGUDfmu13sMDeeaJQpyyS)_

## What this adds

**`brain-core/`**: a plain-Java spiking neural network. It needs no Minecraft and builds and tests on its own with `./gradlew -p brain-core test`.
- About 5,000 leaky integrate-and-fire neurons in an adult (about 3,000 at birth), split into the notebook's lobes: Olfactory, Occipital, Feely, Concept, Emotion, Wernicke's, Memory, Cerebellum and Motor.
- Wiring follows page 111, and Concept and Feely both feed the Cerebellum. Lobe-to-lobe links are topographic, so a map of where things are survives from lobe to lobe.
- Learning: STDP inside the lobes. Cerebellum → motor synapses use a three-factor dopamine rule. Dopamine is a reward prediction error (TD critic over Concept, Emotion and Memory), so only "better than expected" reinforces a key.
- Inborn reflexes that learning builds on: keep the head level, and turn toward a creature it sees.
- Your rules: neurons decay from over- or under-firing, then reset and rewire toward dull, under-connected neurons. Healthy co-firing cements them. Neurons grow with age in the most active lobes. Genes are inherited with crossover and mutation.
- The cerebellum also predicts the next body state, and its error drives curiosity.
- The output is never winner-takes-all: every motor pool is decoded each tick into W/A/S/D, jump, sneak, sprint and continuous mouse look.
- Full save/load (brain file version 2, includes the critic).

**Mod (`src/main`)**
- Senses: 16×10 ray-cast vision in a player's FOV, touch/motion/balance, scents, and pain/pleasure.
- Movement: brain villagers move only through those player inputs. They get a player's speed, sneak speed, sprint rules, air control and sneak edge stop. They keep their own MCA size, and crouching or swimming shrinks them by the same proportions it shrinks a player. Path-finding and look control are switched off for them.
- Brains run on worker threads and are saved to `<world>/reallyalive/brains/<uuid>.brain`.
- Commands: `/reallyalive brain enable|disable|info|babble`, `/reallyalive goal`, and `/reallyalive watch` (keys and lobe activity on the action bar).
- Compatibility: brains are opt-in per villager. There are three narrow mixins that only act on brain villagers, and MCA is an optional dependency.

## Status

- [x] `brain-core` tests: all 15 pass.
- [x] Learning benchmark `MovementLearningTest` passes: after 30k ticks, rewarded brains reach 9.3 goals per 3000 ticks on average (5 to 13 across 6 seeds); unrewarded brains with the same reflexes reach 0.
- [ ] Mod compile and in-game check (in progress on the build side of this branch).
- [ ] Confirm an MCA build for NeoForge 1.21.1 and whether its villagers extend vanilla `Villager`.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

items.title: Harden Gagarin LONG/SHORT directional ranking
items.body:
## Scope
- Require explicit directional evidence from setup, structure, multi-timeframe alignment, or opportunity direction.
- Remove momentum/close-price-only fallback that manufactured directional candidates.
- Reject non-finite numeric values (NaN/Infinity).
- Add regression tests for momentum-only candidates and non-finite inputs.

## Safety
PAPER ONLY. No broker execution, no production deploy, and no merge performed. Await CI and review before integration.

## Follow-up implementation: advisory early-warning ranking + scorecard integrity
- `engine/prediction_ranker.py`: the existing early-warning score can add at most 6 ranking points only when its direction agrees with a direction already established by setup/structure/MTF. Conflicts are surfaced in reasons; early warning cannot create a LONG/SHORT candidate or authorize an entry.
- `main.py`: `_print_ranking()` now prints a separate PAPER advisory ranking from `rank_predictions()`. This is console-only and does not alter governor decisions, execution routing, journal writes, or Telegram messages.
- `telegram/news_monitor.py`: scorecard rejects non-finite/non-positive alert and reaction prices; non-finite/non-positive stop/TP levels are not used to classify outcomes.
- Tests added in `tests/test_prediction_ranker.py` and `tests/test_news_monitor.py` for agreement bonus, no direction manufacture, conflicting early warning, and NaN/Infinity scorecard inputs.
- Commits: `cc3f7bc` (early-warning ranking), `272c373` (main advisory output), `7d7fb12` (ranker tests), `2abec8d` (test discovery fix), `9c40bc0` (finite scorecard validation), `2c8241f` (scorecard regression test).
- CI for commit `7d7fb12`: PAPER, Execution Layer, commodity trade-plan, and NEWS alert jobs reported success; Public Event Brain and SOYUZ GAGARIN integration were still running at last poll. CI for the later scorecard commits has not yet been verified.

## Safety
PAPER ONLY. No merge, production deploy, broker order, or real-message test was performed.

## Follow-up: advisory ranking and finite-value scorecard hardening
- `engine/prediction_ranker.py` now gives at most 6 heuristic points to an early-warning score only when its direction agrees with an existing direction from setup/structure/MTF; conflict is labeled, and early warning cannot create a candidate.
- `main.py` prints a separate PAPER advisory ranking from `rank_predictions`; it does not alter governor decisions, execution, journaling or Telegram.
- `telegram/news_monitor.py` rejects NaN/Infinity/non-positive prices in the alert scorecard and refuses non-finite SL/TP levels for outcome classification.
- Added tests: `tests/test_prediction_ranker.py`, `tests/test_main_advisory_ranking.py`, `tests/test_news_monitor.py`.
- Commits: `cc3f7bc`, `272c373`, `7d7fb12`, `2abec8d`, `9c40bc0`, `2c8241f`, `df0a054`.
- Latest CI at commit `df0a054`: NEWS alert, SOYUZ GAGARIN integration, PAPER and Execution Layer workflows were still running at last poll; the commodity trade-plan tests completed successfully. Earlier runs for `cc3f7bc` and `272c373` completed successfully, but preceded the final scorecard changes.

PAPER ONLY. No merge, deploy, broker order or real Telegram test.

## Follow-up: Telegram alert clarity and trade-plan validation
- `telegram/news_monitor.py`: Telegram news alerts now show the current price, indicative entry, SL, TP1/optional TP2, theoretical risk/reward percentages, and R/R to TP1.
- Before an alert can be sent, numeric price levels must be finite and positive, with SL and TP1 on the correct side of entry for LONG/SHORT. Invalid geometry is rejected rather than sent to Telegram.
- The message explicitly notes that the news impact is heuristic, R/R excludes spread/slippage/gaps, feed prices may differ from Trading 212 CFD quotes, and no order is sent.
- Regression coverage added in `tests/test_news_monitor.py` for message contents, R/R calculation, NaN rejection, and invalid stop/target geometry.
- Commits: `d0fe937` (Telegram message and level validation), `525d820` (tests).
- CI for the latest commit `525d82002b2d94af6eeff15b155bc990bec68bfa` has not returned a workflow result yet. No merge, deploy, real Telegram delivery test, or order execution performed.

PAPER ONLY.

## Follow-up: validate temporal cadence in early-warning lead-time backtest
- `engine/early_warning.py`: the rolling lead-time backtest now rejects the evaluated window when a large timestamp gap makes a bar-count horizon temporally incomparable. It returns `INSUFFICIENT_DATA` rather than reporting a potentially misleading lead-time metric.
- Added explicit `warning_to_favorable_seconds` / `warning_to_adverse_seconds` sample aliases and corresponding median fields. These are elapsed times from the warning to threshold touches, not proof that the warning preceded the beginning of a move.
- Regression coverage in `tests/test_early_warning.py` checks gap rejection and backward-compatible timing aliases.
- Commits: `abcb60f` (cadence guard and explicit timing metrics), `8382102` (regression tests).
- CI for the latest head `8382102272630c43357c08a4abbcb3ae31881b5a`: all six latest PR workflows completed successfully (SOYUZ GAGARIN Tests, PAPER, Execution Layer, NEWS alert, Public Event Brain, and commodity trade-plan tests).

PAPER ONLY. No merge, deploy, live order, or real Telegram delivery test.

## Follow-up: reject boolean values as market data
- `engine/early_warning.py`: `_finite()` now rejects Python booleans rather than accepting `True` as numeric price/timestamp `1.0`. This prevents malformed boolean fields from silently entering the warning calculation or OHLC backtest.
- Regression tests in `tests/test_early_warning.py` cover boolean close prices, timestamps, and OHLC values; invalid rows fail closed with zero samples and no execution authorization.
- Commits: `e8cf890` (input validation), `09a38ab` (regression tests).
- CI at head `09a38ab7ae8f30a4d0c86419568357ad3df07dd5`: all six distinct PR workflows completed successfully. The full Gagarin integration suite reported **395 passed**; the NEWS/Telegram-related suite reported **62 passed**. Duplicate execution/NEWS runs also completed successfully.
- Lead-time metrics remain elapsed time from the warning to a future 0.5-ATR threshold touch; they do not by themselves establish when a move began or prove predictive edge.

PAPER ONLY. No merge, deployment, real order, or real Telegram send was performed.

## Follow-up: identify warnings after a prior 30m move
- `engine/early_warning.py`: each historical warning sample now records `pre_warning_30m_move_atr` and `move_already_underway`, plus aggregate count/percentage of warnings issued after a prior 30-minute move of at least 0.5 ATR.
- This is explicitly a lateness proxy based only on the price history available at warning time; it is not claimed to identify the true onset of a move or prove predictive edge.
- `tests/test_early_warning.py` checks the per-sample classification and aggregate percentage.
- Commits: `6b0f86f` (metric), `969ae7a` (regression assertion).
- CI for `969ae7aaa8c2fef59433a3e4caacc386a3d97094` is pending verification.

PAPER ONLY. No merge, deployment, real order, or real Telegram delivery test performed.

## Follow-up: direction-aware early-warning lateness
- `engine/early_warning.py`: the 30-minute pre-warning move is now reconstructed from the simple return using the exact implied base price, rather than the approximation `entry * return_pct`.
- Added `pre_warning_30m_directional_move_atr` and `prior_move_against_warning`. A warning is counted as potentially late only if the preceding move of at least 0.5 ATR was already in the warning's direction; an opposite move is reported separately as a possible reversal context, not mislabeled as late continuation.
- `tests/test_early_warning.py` verifies the exact return-to-price conversion, direction alignment, threshold classification, and aggregate counts.
- Commits: `a41b12f` (implementation), `56bcc97` (regression tests).
- CI on the updated head is being checked; results will be recorded when completed.

PAPER ONLY. No merge, deploy, real order, or real Telegram delivery test performed.

## Follow-up: measure earlier 0.25 ATR excursions
- `engine/early_warning.py`: the rolling backtest now records warning-to-favorable and warning-to-adverse times for an earlier 0.25 ATR excursion, alongside the existing 0.5 ATR threshold. It reports which side is reached first, same-bar ambiguity, and neither-hit cases.
- `tests/test_early_warning.py`: added regression assertions that the 0.25 ATR outcome categories partition all samples and that the earlier favorable threshold is not later than the 0.5 ATR threshold when both are reached.
- This is an observable excursion proxy, not a claim to identify the true start of a market move. OHLC bars cannot determine intrabar ordering when both thresholds are touched in the same candle.
- Commits: `b9b3338` (metrics), `1e621cd` (regression assertions).
- CI for head `1e621cd479cb6c921bd59a7e25d4a60224ce2d28`: all six PR workflows completed successfully (SOYUZ GAGARIN Tests, PAPER, Execution Layer, NEWS alert, Public Event Brain, and commodity trade-plan tests).

PAPER ONLY. No merge, deploy, broker order, or real Telegram delivery test performed.

## Follow-up: classify warning timing from the prior move
- `engine/early_warning.py`: each rolling backtest sample now receives a `prior_move_timing_class` based only on the 30m move visible at warning time: `LOW_PRIOR_MOVE_PROXY`, `LATE_CONTINUATION_PROXY`, `REVERSAL_CONTEXT_PROXY`, `INTERMEDIATE_PRIOR_MOVE`, or `UNCLASSIFIED`.
- Aggregate counts and rounded percentages are exposed and checked by regression tests. Labels are diagnostic proxies; they do not claim to know the true trend onset or prove predictive edge.
- Commits: `11ab4d4` (classification and aggregates), `4bf1155` (initial regression coverage), `987b901` (robust percentage assertion).
- CI for the latest commit must be checked after GitHub Actions completes.

PAPER ONLY. No merge, deployment, real orders, or real Telegram delivery test performed.

## Follow-up: stratify early-warning outcomes by prior move
- `engine/early_warning.py`: adds outcome summaries by the decision-time-only `prior_move_timing_class`, plus a second breakdown by LONG/SHORT. Each group reports sample count, favorable-first/adverse-first/same-bar/neither 0.5-ATR outcomes, resolved-only favorable-first percentage, median elapsed time to favorable/adverse 0.5 ATR, and median direction-adjusted returns at 3/6/12 bars.
- Empty groups return zero counts and `None` where a percentage or median is undefined. Regression assertions verify that group totals partition the original samples and that LONG/SHORT counts reconcile with each class.
- Commits: `1084014` (aggregation), `1eac408` (regression tests), `75d1700` (expose metrics in result).
- The first CI run caught a missing pair of output keys (398 passed, 1 failed); the return object was corrected. All six workflows on final head `75d170036c19197a250be14a9b1be71bd5d71c91` then completed successfully.

PAPER ONLY. These are historical diagnostics, not calibrated probabilities or evidence of live predictive edge. No merge, deploy, broker order, or real Telegram delivery test performed.

## Follow-up: future-invariance of warning-time metadata
- Extended the walk-forward regression test to change only candles strictly after a cutoff and verify that every warning-time field remains unchanged: 30m return, absolute and directional move in ATR, already-underway/reversal flags, and the prior-move timing class.
- This guards against accidental look-ahead leakage into early-warning timing diagnostics; future candles remain outcome-only.
- Commit: `e4ba8b95ec8ff92d30cd3ed122e65ae7f7a6ed66`.
- All six PR-triggered workflows on this commit completed successfully: SOYUZ GAGARIN Tests, SOYUZ GAGARIN PAPER, Gagarin Execution Layer Tests, Gagarin NEWS alert tests, Gagarin Public Event Brain Tests, and Commodity trade-plan tests.

PAPER ONLY. No merge, deploy, real order, or real Telegram delivery test performed.

## Follow-up: de-overlap early-warning outcome windows
- `engine/early_warning.py`: retains the existing full-sample metrics and adds a secondary diagnostic using a chronological subset whose future outcome windows do not overlap, regardless of whether adjacent warnings are LONG or SHORT.
- Each sample exposes its sorted-series bar index and whether it is included in the non-overlapping diagnostic. The result reports the subset size, excluded overlapping windows, and the same 0.5-ATR outcome summary for that subset.
- `tests/test_early_warning.py`: regression coverage checks the greedy window-selection boundary across direction changes and verifies that selected outcome windows do not overlap and outcome counts still partition the subset.
- Commits: `40e1092` (implementation), `13fbc00` (regression tests).
- All six PR workflows on head `13fbc006602bcdf256fb597cb0750539073a3347` completed successfully: SOYUZ GAGARIN Tests, SOYUZ GAGARIN PAPER, Gagarin Execution Layer Tests, Gagarin NEWS alert tests, Gagarin Public Event Brain Tests, and Commodity trade-plan tests.

PAPER ONLY. The non-overlapping subset is a robustness diagnostic, not an out-of-sample test or proof of predictive edge. No merge, deployment, real order, or real Telegram delivery test performed.

## Follow-up: chronological holdout diagnostics for early-warning lead time
- `engine/early_warning.py`: adds a chronological 75/25 diagnostic split over eligible warning indices when the evaluated span is long enough. Development samples are retained only when their entire future outcome window ends before the split; boundary-crossing samples are excluded. Development and holdout outcomes are de-overlapped independently.
- Each sample records `temporal_validation_partition` for evaluation reporting only; this field does not affect warning direction or execution.
- The result reports development/holdout counts and outcome summaries, the boundary exclusions, and whether the holdout has at least 20 non-overlapping samples. Short windows explicitly return `INSUFFICIENT_DATA` for the split rather than manufacturing a comparison.
- Regression coverage checks partition boundaries, outcome-count reconciliation, and the short-window guard.
- Commits: `a3bd855` (implementation), `d4849d0` (regression tests).
- All six PR workflows on head `d4849d0927d014a4c493817794ce06b7c02aed99` completed successfully. Gagarin integration tests: **405 passed**; NEWS/Telegram-related tests: **68 passed**.
- This is a chronological descriptive diagnostic, not a fitted model, calibrated probability, proof of predictive edge, or full independent market-period study.

PAPER ONLY. No merge, deployment, real order, or real Telegram delivery test performed.

## Follow-up: holdout early-warning metrics by timing class and direction
- `engine/early_warning.py`: adds `temporal_validation.holdout_by_prior_move_class_and_direction`, summarizing only the chronological holdout's non-overlapping outcome windows by decision-time prior-move class and LONG/SHORT direction.
- Short/insufficient series retain the same output schema with zero samples and undefined medians/percentages. The metric is explicitly descriptive and does not change warning generation or execution.
- Regression coverage verifies that nested LONG/SHORT/class counts reconcile to the holdout non-overlapping count and that outcome categories partition every subgroup; short-series output remains empty and safe.
- Commits: `f972d06` (implementation), `933549f` (initial regression assertions), `2c5d355` (make the test independent of the full-sample overlap flag).
- All six PR-triggered GitHub Actions workflows on head `2c5d355eb67fcc78145107509577dd151af54e29` completed successfully: SOYUZ GAGARIN Tests, SOYUZ GAGARIN PAPER, Gagarin Execution Layer Tests, Gagarin NEWS alert tests, Gagarin Public Event Brain Tests, and Commodity trade-plan tests.

PAPER ONLY. No merge, deployment, real order, or real Telegram delivery test performed. The holdout stratification is descriptive; small subgroups do not establish predictive edge.

items.title: fix(gacha-forge): repair story music and choice pre-generation
items.body:
## Linked issue

Closes #1628. Closes #1634. Closes #1635. Follow-up to the Dottore finding posted after #1630 was merged. @SpicyMarinara / Codex owns this work.

## Why this change

Story playback currently falls through to the Home audio cue, so chapters and Character Stories reuse the Home song instead of generating their own tracks. Unanswered small choices also stop later shared narration and pre-forging, even though their alternative branches are already stored together. Audio notices additionally intercept stage taps or interrupt focused reading.

## What changed

- Derive music cues from the actual displayed story state and ready content, preserving the current track during loading.
- Allow shared narration and pre-forging past small choices; retain playback selection, first canon, replay, big-decision locks and safe completion/compression.
- Short notices allow stage taps; overflowing reasons retain native scrolling and keyboard focus.
- Focus pauses notice dismissal; leaving the notice resumes the six-second delay.
- Ship Gacha Forge 1.12.1 with rebuilt payload, manifest, archive, catalogs and release notes. Preserve the published 1.12.0 archive and record the actual merged Engine music baseline.

## Package and security impact

- Affected package IDs: `gacha-forge` (1.12.1).
- Engine compatibility impact: capability API 1.381 remains unchanged; actual host baseline `b9cc386e868d8ab9cdb4826939323a67d464e7bf`.
- New or changed permissions/entrypoints: none.
- Restart, storage, update, or uninstall impact: update the installed package and restart normally; no storage-format changes.

## Validation

- [ ] `node scripts/validate-catalog.mjs` passes locally
- [ ] `git diff --check` passes locally
- [ ] Rebuilt every affected manifest, payload, artifact, and catalog entry

items.title: feat(audio): add adaptive music and selective synth builds
items.body:
## Summary

Games can schedule sounds and adaptive music on the audio clock. Synth instruments render when the game starts; rendering audio files during the build is out of scope.

- **`@yagejs/audio`** plays through native Web Audio and drops `@pixi/sound`. It adds scheduled starts and stops, sample offsets, stereo pan, loop regions, gain, rate and pan automation, child channels, a lookahead scheduler for sequencers, diagnostics, and offline rendering through the same graph. Each sound can carry a sustain loop and a `rootNote`, the MIDI pitch of the recording. Engines in one page share a decoded file until the last of them unloads it.
- **`@yagejs-addons/synth`** adds 25 seeded instruments and noise sources with sustain loops. Pitched instruments report their root note, and `SynthPlugin` registers it with each alias. Instruments are named exports of `@yagejs-addons/synth/instruments`, so an ESM bundle keeps only the instruments it imports. `SynthPlugin` can render in a module worker. The `/render` entry renders without engine imports, for Node scripts, tests and previews.
- **Custom instruments.** `defineInstrument` and the DSP building blocks (`renderString`, `renderModal`, `renderAdditive`, `renderMetal`, `renderNoise`, filters, level tools, `seededRandom`) are public on `/render`. A game-defined instrument works in `SynthPlugin`, a worker and music tracks. Instrument names are type parameters, so an inline `instruments` set rejects a misspelled descriptor at compile time.
- **`@yagejs-addons/music`** (new) plays a repeating song on an entity: tracks of notes, any meter, swing, named parameters that fade layers, transitions on the next bar, and cues moved into the current chord. Notes transpose against each sound's registered root note, so songs need no tuning data.
- **Fixed songs.** A game that does not need adaptive music can render a song once with `renderAudio` and loop the result. The music guide shows the boot code.
- **Adaptive-music example.** One component turns gameplay intents (danger, a reward, a new area, pause) into music. `SynthPlugin` renders its nine sounds at boot. The hi-hat is an instrument the example defines itself.

## API changes

- **Breaking:** a loaded sound asset holds an `AudioBuffer`. Constructing an `AudioManager` directly takes a `BaseAudioContext`.
- **Breaking:** fades run on the audio clock. `fadeTo` returns `void`, and its `easing` option becomes `curve: "linear" | "exponential"`. Cancel a fade with a new volume write or `stop()`. A volume write that replaces a `stopOnComplete` fade also cancels its stop. `crossfade` still returns the incoming handle. It takes no `easing` option and fades linearly.

```ts
// main: fades returned a Process and followed ProcessSystem.timeScale
await handle.fadeTo(0, { duration: 0.6, easing: easeInOutQuad }).toPromise();

// this branch: fades are booked on the audio clock
handle.fadeTo(0, { duration: 0.6, curve: "linear", stopOnComplete: true });
```

Fades on `main` already ignored scene pause and scene time scale. The one behaviour change is that `ProcessSystem.timeScale` does not scale them. A fade is a mixer ramp, so it keeps its length during slow motion and behind a pause menu. To hold a fade, pause the handle or its channel. The remaining automation waits until resume.

`SynthPlugin` stays on the synth package root, so existing synth imports keep working.

A game-defined instrument, in its own module and in boot code:

```ts
import { SynthPlugin } from "@yagejs-addons/synth";
import { flute } from "@yagejs-addons/synth/instruments";
import { defineInstrument, limit, normalize, renderString } from "@yagejs-addons/synth/render";

export const harp = defineInstrument("harp", (frequency, sampleRate, seed) =>
  limit(normalize(renderString(
    { frequency, duration: 1.2, t60: 1, brightness: 0.7, pickPosition: 0.4, seed },
    sampleRate,
  ))),
);

engine.use(new SynthPlugin({ instruments: { flute, harp }, sounds: { pluck: harp.sound() } }));
```

New sound metadata, in a scene or at boot:

```ts
const Pad = sound("/audio/pad.wav", { loopStart: 0.5, loopEnd: 1.5, rootNote: 57 });
audio.getSoundMetadata(Pad); // { loopStart: 0.5, loopEnd: 1.5, rootNote: 57 }
handle.release({ at: audio.currentTime + 2, duration: 0.2 });
```

## Review guide

- The audio backend is the bulk of the change: `packages/audio/src/AudioManager.ts`, `SoundHandle.ts`, `AudioTimeline.ts` (the value planner behind every volume, rate and pan ramp) and `AudioPlugin.ts` (unlock, visibility suspension, the scheduler timer, loaded-sound cleanup). `assets.ts` counts the engines that hold each decoded file.
- The DSP refactor behind the public building blocks leaves every built-in's samples unchanged: 25 instruments at three frequency, seed and sample-rate combinations hash identically before and after.
- `packages/addons/synth/scripts/check-bundles.mjs` runs after the synth build. It fails if a named instrument import pulls in another instrument's renderer, or if `/render` or `/worker` imports the engine.
- The music transport is `packages/addons/music/src/MusicPlayer.ts`. Layer parameters are `AudioTimeline` values mapped onto channel volume ramps.

## Validation

- [x] `npx turbo typecheck`, `npx turbo lint`, `npx turbo test` and `npm run format:check`, including the repository checks
- [x] Docs build, including type-checked snippets
- [x] Synth bundle check after build
- [x] The 25 built-in instruments render identical samples before and after the DSP refactor
- [x] Playwright: `adaptive-music.spec.ts`, and the `audio`, `synth`, `adaptive-music` and `feel-addon` example smoke tests
- [x] Production build of the adaptive-music example, 15 page loads: 14 played every note in the first four seconds, and 1 skipped 2 notes
- [x] `npx changeset status`

items.title: Replay development policies on the sim-v2 archive
items.body:
Stacked on #80 (`study/policy-interface-qualification-20261020`). The base is that branch; retarget to `main` after #80 merges. This PR does not change #80's result files.

The pinned FTG and PP policy replay passes the registered gate on the corrected sim-v2 archive. All 825 evaluation-agent recordings and 167,647 retained rows executed; every row is finite and in support; source densities agree with the stored log densities within 7.7e-5 and the independent calculation agrees with the source within 1.8e-15, against 3.1e-5 and 7.4e-7 on real-v2. Zero terminal rows fail the action-frame gate, and the archive contains no zero `raw_actions` row. Simulation densities agree where real densities agreed, and the terminal zero-target convention that keeps the real action gate open does not occur in simulation, which places it on the real car's recording or safety path. `runs/ope_policy_interface_qualification_sim/result.json` owns the numbers; the new section in `reports/ope_policy_interface_qualification.md` summarizes them.

The sim protocol copies #80's tolerances, configurations, source hashes, observation fields and exclusion rule and changes only the archive identity (Drive object, ZIP hash, the loader's empty bad-trajectory list for this archive). It was committed before the replay. The replay script gained one `--protocol` argument whose default is the real-v2 protocol, so #80's command and result string are unchanged; the real replay was not rerun.

What was run, in Python 3.11 with `requirements-ope-corrected-v2.txt` and the pinned agents checkout:

```
python -m unittest experiments.test_common_reward_v2 experiments.test_simulator_reward_adapter_v2 experiments.test_policy_density_v2
python -m experiments.replay_development_policies_v2 --protocol runs/ope_policy_interface_qualification_sim/protocol.json --real-zip <sim zip> --real-root <sim root> --agents-source <pinned agents> --private-rows <private ledger> --out runs/ope_policy_interface_qualification_sim/result.json
```

Limits: the sim replay admits nothing on the real action gate, which stays failed in #80. Exact stochastic draws remain unreproducible on either archive. No return or ranking was read; M2, M3 and reserved evaluation remain closed. A sim row outside support, a density mismatch beyond the frozen rule, or a zero raw target in the simulation archive would change the conclusion that the convention is specific to the real recordings.

Local checks: 14 reward, bridge and density unit tests passed; structural tests 8 passed with 1 optional skip; presentation checker 117 local links with no issues; presentation tests 4 passed; Python compile and `git diff --check` passed. #80's run files are byte-identical; the private sim ledger stays outside git with its SHA-256 in the result. No AI review was requested for this PR.

Needs owner check:
- Retarget this PR to `main` after #80 merges; review #80 first.
- Whether the unsent author question in the policy report should be narrowed to the real car's terminal-row recording path, now that simulation shows no zero target.
- Whether the sim-v2 archive's float64 previous actions (real-v2 stores float32) matter for any later paired real-versus-simulation comparison.

items.title: Bot: risk-free attack with a counter-bodied creature — prune body-funded shots below the root, sooner win outranks later (issue #3376)
items.body:
Closes #3376

## What was wrong

The Bot declined a risk-free attack with Walking Ballista into an empty board. It **reproduced at HEAD and was seed-sensitive**, measured through `searchWithTrace` at 400 iterations. With 2 counters, 4 lands and an opposing hand of 5, it attacked on 2 of 12 seeds. Every pick was `material-tiebreak` inside `outcomeEps`, with declining ahead by up to 8 margin points. Hill Giant and Grizzly Bears in the same position attacked on 12 of 12 seeds.

**The responsible seam is the subtree evaluation, specifically rollout noise.** It is neither enumeration nor a root tie-break: the attack is enumerated, and the root leaves of the two edges are identical, because no damage is dealt at the declaration.
- The rollout's ε draw (25%) and the tree's own children below the root kept firing "remove a +1/+1 counter: 1 damage to any target". That shot offers one variant per player and creature against a single `pass`.
- Measured over 300 hand-run rollouts per edge, the Ballista's body score fell from about 204 to 63–88.
- A declared attack opens three more bot priority windows (blocks, damage, end of combat). The attack edge therefore lost the body more often (creatures term 62.9 vs 87.8), and its 2 damage (+18) drowned in that loss.

## Changes

1. **`costShrinksSource`** (`ai/abilityTiming.ts`), the partial sibling of `costDestroysSource`. It asks, by simulation through `payRemoveCounterCost` plus the CR 613.4 layer read, whether paying a `removeCounter` cost lowers the source's power or toughness, or removes the source. Spore and charge counters never count as a shrink, and no counter type is hardcoded.
2. **`isSourceBodyDamageConversion`** (`search.ts`), a sibling of the exchange-sacrifice predicates. It matches the bot's own damage-only activation paid out of its body, on an empty stack, and drops it from the ε draw and from the tree's children below the root.
   - The root and the greedy policy are untouched, so a lethal shot or a creature-killing shot is still found.
   - Neither site is enough alone: ε draw only → the 1-counter case attacks on 3 of 12 seeds; tree only → the hand-holding case attacks on 7 of 12.
3. **A sooner win outranks a later one** (`scoreLeaf(…, since)`, the owner's call). Without the noise, the existing must entry `activation payoff: shoots its own last counter at a face on 1` (issue #3192) went red: `pass` → lethal attack with the Ballista alive out-scored the shot now (0.938 vs 0.915), because `evaluate` orders wins by material. The pre-fix pass sat at 0.76 only because its subtree shot the Ballista away in a quarter of its lines.
   - A won leaf's height above the band floor is scaled by `0.85^steps` elapsed since the root, floored at 0.5. This touches the **reward only**: the tie-break margin stays pure material (issue #138), like `evaluate`'s race and combat terms.
   - Two discarded designs failed on measured entries:
     - A subtracted cost pinned every win a turn away to the band floor (Sylvan Safekeeper's sacrifice tied `pass`, the saturation ADR 0102 describes).
     - An unfloored decay compressed a win next turn to about a tenth of its height, which reddened `decking: casts the storm kill that recurs its own Black Lotus`.
   - Charging the margin as well reddened `known top: plays the creature instead when the known top is a blank`.

Card-agnostic throughout (ADR 0102). No root rule was added. The hold rules are not modified.

## Review (one round, opus)

- Applied: the stale snapshot pins were re-recorded (below); the saturation finding led to the decay design; stale comments were fixed; the clock's behaviour across an additional combat phase is documented.
- Not applied: exempting a lethal shot from the tree prune. Measured, it handed `pass` a win one step later, which `hold-trick` read as outcome-equal to shooting now. The lethal shot stays pruned below the root, as the siblings' lethal drains and burns are, and the root still weighs it at every real decision.
- Not applied: memoizing `costShrinksSource` (perf). The searchCost pins below show no material per-iteration change.

## Measured after the fix

- The attack is taken on 12 of 12 seeds at 1, 2 and 3 counters, with 0, 2, 4 and 6 lands, with or without a hand on either side.
- All 9 Walking Ballista blade entries are green.
- `test:blade`: green (298 passed).
- `bunx vitest run --project bot-node --project bot-dom`: 4077 passed, 1 failed. The failure is `weightFit.bot.test.ts`, already red on base and tracked by health issue #6558. Note for that refit: this PR adds one blade `moves` verdict.

## Blade entries (must, Minimal Pair)

- Anchor: `discriminating pair: does NOT attack with Walking Ballista into an untapped Hill Giant` (conditional; card discriminant). Green before and after the fix.
- Half: `discriminating pair: attacks with a counter-bodied Walking Ballista into an empty board`. Red before the fix.

## Re-pinned (the change is meant to move the search)

- `searchLeafScore.snapshot.json` (`RECORD_LEAF_SNAPSHOT=1`) and the `evaluateManaCensus` snapshot (depletion-land position).
- `searchForcedPass` medium root digest: `b76aa909e9f2b32c` → `00d9cf06ffe288af`. The chosen move and the RNG counter are unchanged.
- `searchCost` medium, at 100 iterations:

| counter | before | after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| iterations | 97 | 96 |
| clones | 388 | 391 |
| enumerations | 629 | 620 |
| evaluations | 291 | 294 |
| sbaSweeps | 2192 | 2175 |
| censuses | 734 | 739 |
| searchDraws | 5739 | 5679 |

  Per-iteration work is flat: 4.00 → 4.07 clones per iteration.
- `rootRuleMoratorium`'s end-to-end knob test moved from `standing-spend-hold` to `hold-trick` on "holds a sacrifice engine through its own main phase", where the flip with the rule disabled is measured. The Ballista end-step entry now holds with `standing-spend-hold` off. That is a possible retirement, written up in `docs/findings/3376-standing-spend-hold-may-be-inert.md`, not acted on.
- `data/blade-card-index.json` and `data/blade-reproducers.json` were regenerated.

## Tests + proof-of-failure

`convex/gre/ai/__tests__/sourceBodyDamageConversion.bot.test.ts`: 9 tests. Every mutation below was asserted applied, run after all edits, and reverted:

| mutation | went red |
| --- | --- |
| prune forced off | unit "prunes…" + blade `attacks with a counter-bodied Walking Ballista…` |
| `costShrinksSource`'s P/T comparison forced false | 2 unit tests + the same blade entry |
| empty-stack clause dropped | unit "made in response" |
| `since` ignored | unit win-timing + blade `shoots its own last counter at a face on 1` |
| margin charged too | unit "margin stays pure material" |
| decay unfloored (measured during design) | blade `decking: … Black Lotus` |

`check:ts`, `check:test-hygiene` and `cr:lint` are green.

check:ui: no walk owed (no `src/**` change; the diff cannot reach the DOM)

Bot reachability: not applicable. No new card or Op; the change is in the search, and the blade entries above cover it.

## Preset scenario

```json
{
  "label": "Bot attacks with a counter-bodied Walking Ballista into an empty board (issue #3376)",
  "spec": {
    "cards": [
      { "name": "Walking Ballista", "owner": "opp", "zone": "battlefield", "summoningSick": false, "counters": { "+1/+1": 2 } }
    ],
    "phase": "PRECOMBAT_MAIN",
    "turn": 5,
    "activePlayer": "opp",
    "landCount": 4,
    "libraryCount": 20
  }
}
```

items.title: feat(rewards): essence ledger, mission catalog and rules engine
items.body:
## Summary
First slice of the rewards system: a currency ("Esencia", `essence` in code) earned through daily and weekly missions and spent on cosmetics. This PR lays the foundations only; nothing is exposed at runtime yet.

- `essence_ledger`: append-only movements, unique on `(user_id, kind, reference_key)` so a retried credit or purchase never double-applies. The balance is `SUM(delta)` and is never stored.
- `mission_catalog`: `rule` and `reward` are JSON, so a new mission (or a future cosmetic reward for event missions) is a row, not a migration. `name` and `description` hold the player-facing copy per language (`en` mandatory and fallback, `es`); the API resolves it from `Accept-Language`. Seeded with five daily missions (three rotate per day) and three weekly ones.
- Rules engine `evaluateMatch`: a pure function over match facts and per-user state. No I/O, no clock. Periods are keyed by UTC day and ISO week. Daily selection is a deterministic hash of the day key.

## Why
Match results are written to the shared Postgres by the game server; the API never ingests them. The next slice adds a worker in this API that reads `matches` by cursor and feeds this engine, so the game server stays untouched. Keeping the engine pure lets the worker, the tests and a historical backfill share one implementation.

Both migrations live in the cosmetics DataSource (`cosmetics_migrations`). Spec: `odd/tasks/essence-rewards.md`.

## Follow-ups (stacked on main)
1. Worker with cursor over `matches` and progress projection.
2. Missions, essence and shop endpoints.
3. Achievement credit and docs.

## Verification
- `bun test tests/unit/modules/rewards`: 31 pass (RED observed before each implementation).
- `bun test`: 754 pass.
- `bun run lint`, `bun run build`: clean.
- Migrations not yet run against a database.

items.title: vigil-coord status
items.body:
Maintained by **vigil-coord**. Updated after every step.

## ⚠ Phase 1 done-when pending ParkAgent run
Deferred, not waived. It must complete against `main` before phase 2's PR is opened. You name the ParkAgent issue once ParkAgent's fleet has drained its PRs.

## Current phase
**Phase 2a: the pipeline**: the Opus worker is building on `feat/phase-2a` (plan: `docs/plans/phase-2a.md`). Phase 1 is merged as #7, with its ParkAgent done-when pending.

**Phase 1: core** (history). Draft **#7**; CI green. Review round 1 sent it back with 4 blockers and 18 should-fix items; the worker is fixing them (review send-back 1 of 2). The ParkAgent done-when run waits for the fixes and your go-ahead.

### Review round 1: blockers
1. **vigild runs host git inside a `.git` the worker can write.** A planted `commondir`, hook or `insteadOf` could run code on the Mac, or send the push token elsewhere. The reviewer reproduced the hook.
2. **The scope check can be bypassed.** Renames, and a forged `origin/<base>` ref in the worker's clone.
3. **Spec, plan and harness files are read through symlinks.** A coordinator could get `~/.config/vigil/env` stored as an artifact.
4. **Acceptance passes when the test harness couldn't run** (exit 127, or a missing file). ParkAgent's dev image has no pnpm, so its tests would never actually run.

Should-fix highlights:
- The gateway forwards any request body, including server tools and `mcp_servers`, which is egress around smokescreen.
- The budget pre-check misses in-flight calls.
- No crash recovery, so reservations leak and eat the daily cap.
- Repo visibility is trusted from YAML.
- Jev calls aren't metered.
- No resume route.
- The UI isn't bound to Tailscale only.

Full list: `review-p1-round1.md` in the coord scratchpad.

items.title: Retain best PPO checkpoint: verified 10/10 balance trials
items.body:
PPO's final checkpoint regresses after an earlier policy has already learned nominal balance. In a controlled 20,480-step run, the final policy averaged 3.19 seconds with 2/10 successes. Selecting checkpoints on separate validation seeds retains the step-1,024 policy, which achieved 10.00 seconds in all 10 evaluation trials and all 10 additional seeds. The historical approximately 1.30-second result was supplied as context; its model was unavailable for independent verification.

- Select after actual PPO updates using seeds 2000–2009; retain the earliest checkpoint on ties and save the final policy separately.
- Record per-trial outcomes, package/source/model provenance, and an optional strict 10/10 evaluation gate. Physics, reward, observation shape, reset distribution, and fall thresholds are unchanged.
- Include the verified policy and comparison reports in `experiments/balance-checkpoint-selection/`, plus its 501-frame replay in `viewer/trained-robot.json`.
- Preserve the Android viewer implementation. Deploy the reviewed replay from the commit instead of overwriting it with a hardcoded historical Actions artifact.
- Update the existing training workflow to use CPU PyTorch, a bounded 20,000-step default and 20-minute timeout, tests, checkpoint history, and strict evaluation.

Validation: 10 local tests passed, including an actual PPO training/checkpoint reload test and the ten-trial policy regression. Fresh baseline and checkpoint-selection training completed; final-policy parameters match exactly across the two runs, isolating checkpoint selection as the change. Selected policy achieved 10/10 at seeds 1000–1009, 10/10 validation at 2000–2009, and 10/10 additional evaluation at 3000–3009. Replay schema and model hash were checked. See the experiment README for individual reports and reproduction commands.

GitHub Actions validation passed on commit `a247941`: [Train balance AI run 40040929674](https://github.com/ttinorua/ai-robot-lab/actions/runs/40040929674). items.title: fix(average-reward): stabilize GTD secondary RMS

labels.name: needs-human-review
labels.description: Claude triage: controversial, needs a human

items.body:
## Problem

`DifferentialGTDLearner.update` publishes the RMS of its secondary weights with a direct float32 mean of squares. A valid committed state containing several large but finite weights can overflow only in that reduction, so the update reports an infinite metric even though the state and true RMS are finite.

## Change

- preserve the existing direct RMS arithmetic for ordinary values
- use a max-scaled RMS fallback only when the direct result is non-finite and every input weight is finite
- add an end-to-end Differential GTD regression with eight finite `7e18` secondary weights

This is a runtime telemetry correctness fix. It does not change learning state or promote scientific evidence.

## Failing-test-first proof

Before the production change, the regression showed `update_applied == true` but `metrics[5] == inf`. After the change, the same committed update reports the representable `7e18` RMS.

## Validation

- focused large-RMS, rejection, and scan-metric tests — 3 passed
- average-reward and Baird suites — 123 passed
- `python -m ruff check .` — passed
- `python -m mypy` — passed, 226 source files

## Evidence scope

`average_reward.py` is registered in the frozen continual-IA historical chain. The registry is already invalid on current `main` because of pre-existing registered-source drift. This PR does not restore, rerun, or promote that claim, and its tests are not scientific evidence.

Source fixes and passing tests alone do not close a quest. The [quest review guide](https://github.com/RSPSApp/tsps/blob/feat/quest-helper-728/server/docs/agents/quest-testing.md) documents helper/cache preflight, actual packet/dialogue contracts, routing, permitted ordinary setup/boss aids, persistence and checkpoint reuse. This PR stays draft until the active scope's required work is complete.

items.title: [项目裁决索引] 决策、取舍与替代关系（按时间顺序）
items.body:
本 Issue 索引项目工程决定、技术取舍及其替代关系。详细技术合同与原始理由见各条来源及所属 Issue。

当前保留 **286 条工程裁决**。固定 D 编号沿用原值；编号不连续不表示内容缺失，既有编号不重新分配。

## 阅读约定

- 先按主题或固定 D 编号定位条目，再回读来源及所属 Issue 当前合同。索引不替代任务合同或执行授权。
- 日期未记载的条目单列；有日期条目保留原有从早到晚的顺序。同日没有准确时刻时，不由排列推断效力。
- 评论创建、迁移和编辑时间不等于用户作决定的时间，不以这些时间补造裁决日期。
- 只按明确的适用范围判断继承、补充或替代；较新的日期不自动撤销旧决定。历史版本与有限验收不冒充当前完整交付。

items.body:
## **User description** Stacked on #261. Billing groundwork for referral rewards. Plan: `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-10-24-attribution-and-referral.md`. ## What - `lib/billing/reward.ts` - `planReward` (pure) and `grantReward` give N free months without changing what anyone pays. Which lever moves depends on the account: - **Trial:** `trialEndsAt` moves a month later, so a web subscription made later still starts charging at the new trial end. - **Renewing on Google Play:** RevenueCat `defer` pushes the next charge back, then `refreshFromProvider` re-reads the subscription. If the defer fails, it falls back to a gift after the paid period. - **Anything else** (a gift already running, lapsed, a plan that won't renew, or a renewing Razorpay/PayPal plan): a `comp` gift that starts after the latest of now, the running gift and the paid period. Per the decision, a renewing web subscriber's month is **banked after their paid period, never refunded**. - Each reward writes an `admin_audit` row (`billing.reward`, actor `system:referral`). - `grantComp` is lifted out of the admin gift action, which now uses it (same behaviour). - **Fix: the retention clock ignored gifts.** `accessEndedAt` now includes `comp.until`, so a long gift's deletion deadline can't already be past, which used to skip the 30/7/1-day warnings. - **Fix: buying during a gift charged immediately.** Razorpay and PayPal subscribe now start charging when the gift ends, the same as they already did for a trial (`freeUntil`). The plan picker copy follows. ## Tests (written first) - **Planner:** one case per state, plus month-end clamping and sandbox purchases. - **`grantReward` against an in-memory Mongo:** - holds when setup never finished - a trial extension writes an audit row - a Play defer calls RevenueCat's `/subscriptions/envelope_individual/defer` with `expiry_time_ms`, then refreshes - a 400 from the defer falls back to a gift - **Retention:** a gift is counted. - **Razorpay subscribe on a gift:** `start_at` is the gift's end. - Full suite passes (3,541). ## Rollout - Before relying on Play deferral, check that `REVENUECAT_SECRET_KEY` has write permission, using a sandbox subscription on staging. - Exercised end to end by the referral PR that follows. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) ___ ## **CodeAnt-AI Description** **Grant referral months while preserving existing free and paid time** ### What Changed - Referral rewards extend an active trial, delay the next charge for renewing Google Play plans, or add gifted time after existing paid or gifted access ends. Renewing web subscribers receive their reward after their paid period. - Starting a Razorpay or PayPal subscription during a gift now delays the first charge until the gift ends. - Gifted access now counts toward account-retention timing, so deletion warnings are not skipped during long gifts. ### Impact `✅ Referral rewards preserve existing paid time` `✅ No gifted time lost when subscribing early` `✅ Gifted accounts receive deletion warnings on time`

items.title: Orchestrator: DAPO dynamic sampling, dispatch windowing, memory release, and unfiltered reward metrics
items.body:
## Summary
- **DAPO Dynamic Sampling (`--dynamic_sampling` / `filter_zero_variance`)**: Filters out zero-variance prompt groups (`0/G` or `G/G`) in `critique_stage` before `create_trainer_payloads`, replacing them with lightweight metadata stubs (`routed_experts=None`, token arrays cleared) and immediately calling `_release_host_memory()`.
- **Dispatcher Replenishment & Group-Level Windowing (`--max_dispatch_ahead_batches`)**: Advances `max_allowed_prompt_idx` by `_dropped_groups_count` and wakes the dispatcher when a group is dropped in `arrival` mode; scales `iter_prompt_items` by 4x when `dynamic_sampling` is enabled so prompt supply is not exhausted early.
- **Orchestrator OOM Prevention**: Clears `routed_experts`, `prompt_tokens`, `completion_tokens`, `action_mask`, and `payload` on stale/filtered items in `trajectory_queue_manager.build_filter`, and invokes `_release_host_memory()` (`gc.collect()` + `malloc_trim(0)`) after each pipelined micro-batch train step.
- **Unfiltered vs. Kept Reward Metrics & Pass-Rate Logging**: Logs `rewards/mean` across all valid generated rollouts (including filtered zero-variance groups), `rewards/kept_mean` (`rewards/train_kept_mean`) over trained groups, `rollout/filtered_all_correct_groups`, `rollout/filtered_all_wrong_groups`, and optional `--pass_rate_log_path` JSONL part-file logging.
- **Per-Token IS Ratio Cap (`tunix/rl/algo_core.py`)**: Caps per-token `log_is_raw` at `log(5.0)` inside `truncated_importance_weights` to prevent single-token MoE routing outliers from causing gradient spikes under `seq-mask-tis`.

items.title: Explore a 4B event coprocessor with real worker returns and scoped repair
items.body:
Autonomous scientific workers can leave diagnostic streams and emerging blockers unattended. This research package observes real public worker activity and simulation logs, then routes a 4B policy's alerts through existing help/director workflows or a fresh independent repair judge. The judge can grant only a scoped, expiring repair to a private test component; host validation and isolated checks precede application.

The branch contains the event monitor, resident decision serving, rule/periodic baselines, real Codex/WarpX trials, sampled-return export, a bounded LoRA policy-gradient learner, and reproducible experiment records. Production monitoring and supervisor modification are not enabled. The merged helper feature remains PR #45.

Validation and findings:
- 37 local contract tests pass, including real Bubblewrap checks, grant scope/expiry, rollback, provenance after judge retry, sampled behavior records and worker continuation. CI includes these tests without model downloads.
- 20 main real-worker trajectories ran 52 WarpX simulations. A clean sampled incident demonstrated model-origin judge dispatch, scoped repair and continuation of the original worker.
- Four clean sampled episodes supplied 119 decisions for an actual eight-step LoRA update. Prompt/behavior checks, nonzero gradients, exact saved-adapter reload and retrieved artifact hashes passed.
- Four fresh base/adapter trajectories reported diagnostics correctly with no monitor errors. Both policies always deferred: no learned routing benefit was observed.
- Both base and adapted policies now run locally on the RTX 4000 Ada, matching the A100 action on 24/24 checks each. Resident VRAM was about 8.6 GiB and median warm decision latency 4.0/4.6 seconds while another simulation used the GPU. Probabilities differed across devices; this is not a calibration or throughput claim.
- Initial comparison confounds, premature/repeated escalation, incomplete usage accounting and the limits of the feedback-closure reward are documented. No superiority over rules or benefit from RL is claimed.

Read `research/evaluations/monitor-coprocessor-20261023/RESULTS.md` for the evidence and limitations, and `REPRODUCE.md` for replay. Raw traces, weights and training state remain local and outside Git. All weights and training artifacts were retrieved and hash-verified. Colab is stopped with zero active assignments; the reported balance decrease was 23.15 CU. All experimental workers and model processes have exited. This PR remains a draft for research review, not production deployment.


Follow-up reward-design review (24 October):
- A primary-source literature review relates this task to sequential expert deferral, counterfactual credit assignment, LLM routing costs and reward shaping.
- An exact-view audit found case-labelled trial identifiers in 64/119 actual inputs. Removing only the binary feedback condition reduces the analysis-family return gap from 1.04044 to 0.04044; this is reward-definition sensitivity, not a causal worker comparison.
- New sampled/evaluation trial directories are opaque, with case/treatment mappings retained in host manifests. Legacy trajectories and model weights remain frozen.
- A separate paired scorer checks common observations, worker configuration, scientific criteria and budgets, and withholds scores when waiting outcomes or measurements are missing. It is not yet connected to a forked live collector.

Read `research/evaluations/monitor-reward-20261024/REVIEW.md` and its prospective protocol before collecting or training further. No new model improvement is claimed by this follow-up.

The final unfulfilled help request in the analysis episode was worker-initiated, verified from its public creation event. The corrected report retains the original reward and does not treat that request as proven unnecessary. Paired comparison eligibility also requires an identical downstream interaction policy and remains separate from on-policy optimizer eligibility.

items.title: Pet Park: configure 10–25 pets per building, migrate existing capacities safely
items.body:
## Scope: Pet Park building capacity 10–25 (first step of [Pet Park v2 #942](https://github.com/theparadoxicalcollective/Para-Pets/issues/942))

The user clarified that the **overall park scene** should support *up to 100 visibly rendered pets*, but each **building should hold 10–25** pets, set by the admin. Those numbers represent separate limits and should **not** be conflated.

### Changes
- In the Home-style Add Building UI and contextual Edit Building UI, permit **any integer capacity 10–25**, with quick choices 10/15/20/25.
- Centralize 10–25 validation in the shared capacity contract and both admin POST/PATCH endpoints; default newly created buildings to **10**.
- **Migrate existing 1–3-pet buildings safely:** drop old database check, increase legacy lower capacities to **10** (no occupants displaced), update column default, and add `CHECK (max_pets BETWEEN 10 AND 25)`. The migration is additive and idempotent.
- Preserve the transactional occupancy guard from #938: capacity cannot be lowered below current occupants, and conflicting updates are atomic (HTTP 409).
- Preserve **three slots per player** and existing 2,500/5,000-coin unlock costs. Do not change deposited pets, reward accrual/claims, scene layout or online presence in this PR.

### Verification
- Route-level handler tests: create 10/20/25; reject 0/3/9/26/fraction/strings; PATCH at occupancy accepted, below occupancy rejected; invalid values rejected without starting transaction; existing 1–3 upgraded in migration while player slot limit unchanged.
- Required CI: TypeScript, test types, full tests, production build.
- Manual device and DB QA required after deployment: existing legacy building becomes 10; create/edit 10/15/25; test several owners and a reduction while occupied; verify reward ledger and 3-slot limits.
- **Important:** This PR does not implement the new overall 100-pet visible population, presence policy, idle tiles, or exchange flow. Those are sequenced in #942, one verified PR at a time, to avoid stacking behavior changes before regression evaluation.

items.title: Pet Park v2: three earning slots, online-priority 100-pet scene, reward-safe exchange
items.body:
## Goal
Redesign Pet Park so players have **three equipment/earning slots**, while the public park can show **at most 100 small pets** and buildings allow **10–25 pets** (admin configurable). Online players get priority. Pets not on screen **keep accruing and claiming rewards**. Keep Home Bundle-style art/interaction; do not reintroduce the old 390×844 stage.

## Confirmed existing behavior and missing pieces (audit on 2026-10-23)
- The per-player max-three deposits, purchased slots 2/3, hatched/unlisted ownership validation, 24-hour claim cap, fractional reward ledger, safe collect/withdraw endpoints, normalized room positions, deterministic park crowd placement, viewport culling, and public pet animator already exist.
- **Not yet implemented**: park-wide 100 visible-pet selection, authoritative online presence/last activity, explicit displayed-vs-idle state for deposits, reward projections beside each slot, rich pet picker with rarity/adornments/mini-pets, return/exchange flow, owner drag from slot to park, and admin-free equipment view.
- Rendering all deposited pets today is unbounded; PetAnimator at the current scale is relatively large. Home Bundle/World Map patterns should guide scene-based dragging. Existing `PetAnimator` handles public adornments; confirm mini-pet composition instead of assuming it does.
- Existing PR #941 (originally 1–100) should be **updated to 10–25** and merged/passed before new PRs. Its DB migration must upgrade legacy 1–3 building capacities safely without changing deposit ownership, rewards, or the per-player three-slot rule.

## Behavior contract
1. **Three bottom-center tiles** only for normal players while park is open; admin retains scene editing but does not need personal deposit controls. First tile unlocked. Slots 2 & 3 show their *existing* coin costs, 2,500 and 5,000, and use existing purchase policy. The idle tile shows pet artwork, name, stars, level, accumulated coins/essence and Claim. When pet is publicly displayed, the tile artwork is muted/greyed while Claim stays accessible.
2. Tapping an empty unlocked tile opens a filtered **hatched, unlisted, owned pet** picker; artwork must show evolved form, adornments and equipped mini-pets using existing pet-rendering composition. Pet selection is per-slot (no shared global selection race). Verify size/performance on iOS/Android/tablets/portrait PC.
3. Depositing equips into tile/idle state; no public-world placement is required for accrual. Drag the owned pet from its tile onto the **actual panned park world** to make it visible/interactable; normalized placement saves. Tap a placed pet for Return to slot (still earning) or Exchange (collect all unclaimed rewards + withdraw via **existing atomic settlement**, then open filtered picker). Canceling exchange does not remove pet. Never settle by changing only client state.
4. A deposited pet is **reward-eligible** irrespective of idle, indoors, hidden by view cap, or offline owner. A hidden pet still occupies its equipment slot until owner exchanges/retrieves it. Keep current 24-hour earning limit, ledger, exact coin/essence/XP settlement, rate-pause behavior, and rollback/idempotency.
5. **100 is an upper bound on publicly rendered park pets, not number deposited or earning**; prioritize intentionally placed pets belonging to players with verified recent online activity. When slots are available, fall back to earlier eligible offline placed pets in stable order. If cap exceeded, hide lower-priority pets without withdrawal, data loss, or reward changes. Do not shuffle/hide an online pet just because another offline pet arrived.
6. Define online from actual authenticated server activity (NOT merely having a deposit or an open stale login session). Recommended starting policy: a lightweight throttled heartbeat ~60s while authenticated and app visible; activity considered recent for ~10 min, falling back to idle/nonpriority after timeout; update from reliable account-wide activity if already implemented. Avoid per-frame DB writes, client spoofing, unbounded queries, or leaked user activity/presence details.
7. **Scene pets should be visibly smaller** than currently, with camera/world-relative sizing across iOS/Android/portrait PC and performance budget. Park interactions should not interfere with pinch/pan, admin object movement, or building entry. Use viewport culling in addition to 100-pet cap. Indoor building pets require separate sensible capacity handling (10–25 per building) and stable room layout.

## PR sequence / acceptance gates (do not stack on a failing PR)
- [ ] **A. Capacity (#941)** – 10–25 admin setting on create/edit, migrations upgrading legacy low capacities safely; guard reductions below occupants; per-player slots unchanged.
- [ ] **B. Reward-safe slot state** – explicit idle/visible field (additive migration) and owner-only equip/return/placement endpoints; no new reward ledger. Add transactional edge-case tests.
- [ ] **C. 3-slot tile UI + picker** – Home-style centered compact cards, first +, locked prices, hatched pet rich visuals incl evolution/adornments/mini pets, visible greyed art, clear Claim, return/exchange confirmation and atomic reward settlement.
- [ ] **D. Online-first 100-visitor roster** – authenticated, throttled activity, deterministic capped visibility, online priority and expiry, stable offline fallback, size/culling/performance tests. No change to earning based on visibility.
- [ ] **E. Multi-device and multi-account regression** – two accounts active/inactive; >100 deposits; online/offline rotations; indoor capacity; park pan and drag; 24h cap and fractional rewards; offline claims; slow/rejected purchases and requests; repeated exchange/cancel; admin/no personal slots; mobile/desktop real-device QA.
Each PR must follow the Stricter Development Process: trace existing state/APIs, compare known working patterns, minimal complete edit, interaction tests beyond source assertions where feasible, CI + real-device distinction, review regressions before next PR, and retire conflicting old UI only after replacement parity.

## Design decisions awaiting actual usage tests
Use ~10 minutes as a starting inactivity threshold (configurable after feedback). Idle vs public placement must be independent of who is online; timeout changes **public visibility/activity**, not pet ownership or reward eligibility. Never advertise that an offline pet stopped earning.

## Resolution rule
Track each checkbox as implemented, merged, deployed, and manually verified **separately**. Merging is not evidence of device behavior or Railway production rollout.

items.title: test: prove cargo receipt and prepared-command isolation across pwipe

It uses the existing trade policy, codec, SQL executor and normal critical repository. Existing identity/preimage checks suffice; no runtime epoch field or generic cutoff is added.

Diff and commit hooks passed. This test/documentation-only chunk reuses existing build and five-minute gameplay evidence.

items.title: Pressure: how fast a player first pushed counts
items.body:
Pressure gets a fourth part, **First push** (10%). The weights are now 35% army on the map, 40% army sent, 15% damage done and 10% first push.

- **First push:** the first time an attack did damage. That's either an enemy villager killed (the villager estimate, or the unit-by-unit early kills) or an enemy building razed. A building counts as razed when it was attacked and its owner never used it again: no training, research or gather point within 3 minutes of the last hit, and not in the last 5 minutes. An army that walked in and did nothing doesn't count.
- **Scoring:** by the clock, not against the lobby. Damage by 8:00 scores 10, falling to 1 at 30:00, and never pushing also scores 1. A late push isn't rewarded just because nobody else pushed.
- **Explain analysis:** shows e.g. *First push 2:11 → 10 (first damage: a villager of Lathkore's killed at 2:11)*.
- ANALYSIS_VERSION 64.

**On game 515737316:**
- link_chaos: 2:11 (scout kill) → 10
- Mr. X: 9:03 → 9.6
- MODI: 9:33 → 9.4
- PEPPA: 16:25 → 6.6

Players whose kills the bot can't see get 1. The villager estimate misses some kills.

items.title: Add Bounty Hunter with target rewards and crater bots
items.body:
Adds playable Bounty Hunter in Daimon's Crater, reached through Ferox Enclave, with a safe lobby, target matchmaking, combat rules, coffers, rewards and the minigame HUD.

- Implements target kills, BH points, emblems, earning potential, bounty and supply crates, the reward shop, risk skulls and Teleport to Target.
- Spawns a shared random population of 20–50 BhBots when a player enters the lobby. Bots use the shared PvP engine, fund their minimum coffer, keep their skulls and respawn after death. The population is removed when the last real player leaves the crater.
- Uses normal server death loot for crater bots and makes the shared PvP brain retaliate against actual attackers without losing the separate BH assignment. Rogue attacks follow OSRS's ±5-level restriction; assigned targets use matchmaking eligibility.
- Keeps distant target arrows on the minimap, removes the shared minimap-arrow distance cutoff and clears stale hints on login.

Validation: server build and 136 server tests pass (bot brain, Bounty Hunter and items kept on death); client typecheck and both hint-arrow/attack-timer tests pass. Live MCP checks covered population creation/cleanup and attack permissions; a client screenshot verified the distant target arrow. The three-way retaliation scenario is covered by regression tests but has not been visually replayed.

OSRS reference: [Bounty Hunter combat and rogue-level rules](https://secure.runescape.com/m=news/bounty-hunter-is-back?oldschool=1).
